style: Compact, defensively resolute side that frustrates opponents and looks to strike on set pieces and quick counters. Under Sabri Lamouchi, organised out of possession with a rejuvenated, energetic midfield.
recent_form: Qualified comfortably from CAF Group H. New coach Lamouchi took over in January 2026 and has refreshed the squad, blending experience with younger profiles ahead of the tournament.

key_players.name: Ellyes Skhiri
key_players.note: Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder and the most significant cog in midfield; the only Tunisian to play Champions League football this season.

key_players.name: Hannibal Mejbri
key_players.note: Burnley man forming an efficient midfield partnership with Achouri; energetic and creative.

key_players.name: Elias Achouri
key_players.note: FC Copenhagen midfielder who drives the team's tempo and link play.

key_players.name: Aymen Dahmen
key_players.note: Consistent shot-stopper who has been reliable for the national team in recent years.

key_players.name: Ismael Gharbi
key_players.note: 21-year-old PSG academy product, mesmerising on the ball with skills and tricks.

key_players.name: Youssef Msakni
key_players.note: Tunisia's second-most-capped player and third-highest scorer; experienced wide attacker.

historical_news: Sabri Lamouchi took over as head coach in January 2026 and reshaped the squad.
Tunisia drawn in a tough group with the Netherlands, Japan and Sweden.
Captain Ellyes Skhiri the only Tunisian to feature in the Champions League this season.
Lamouchi placed trust in newer, younger player profiles for the World Cup.
Veteran Youssef Msakni recalled despite being absent from the recent AFCON squad.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Modest expectations given the low ranking and a brutal group draw, though the new coach's rebuild and Skhiri's leadership offer cautious encouragement.
